items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: Another name I came across in the Union book was Louis Peterson, but he worked for the Boot and Shoe Workers.

ctx.x: Bill Krieger was one of the finest, clandest men I've ever heard. That's saying a lot now. Because I worked with Bill and when I had the band out at the roadhouse, the Thomas Roadhouse, he was working in Morton's out in Bucktown. That was up on the second floor, they had Morton's restaurant on the bottom dancing up top there. He was working up there with, let's see, I think he was working with Louis Frey was playing piano, Leslie Allen I believe was playing. Man, that's a guy who can play good fiddle. Nobody ever…

I like what little I've heard of him on record. Oh man, he played good. He sure did. Well, was Don Peterson any kind of you, the super-comer player? No, no, no, no, no, no. Another name I came across in the Union book was Louis Peterson, but he worked for the Boot and Shoe Workers. He would come and plead that the musicians should buy Union shoes and Union boots.

Yeah, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. Don Don played. Funny thing, I believe we had a brother by the name of Harold Peterson too. Yeah, we used to play with all those times. He sure did. We lived on Broadway and they lived on Broadway.
